content:
maria: quick heads-up — the go quickstart generator sample hangs when I cancel the context during the initial handshake. repro is tiny and happens reliably on my laptop. :confused:

sam: which SDK version? any stack?

maria: go 1.20 + our go-sdk v0.13.2. minimal repro below. it blocks on Close() and I see a goroutine leak in `pprof`:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 3*time.Second)
defer cancel()

gen := client.Generator("gpt-open", opts...)
for gen.Next(ctx) {
    out := gen.Value()
    fmt.Println(out.Text)
}
// expect this to exit but it stalls here until timeout
gen.Close()
```

logs: 
```
panic-like: runtime: goroutine leaked: net/http: request canceled
goroutine 42 [select]:
  runtime.gopark(...)
```

leo: hmm. sounds like the handshake goroutine is started by Generator() and doesn't observe the cancel propagated from Next(ctx) until after the first token arrives. so Close() waits on a handshake/streamer that never finishes.

jen: are you using the iterator-style `Next(ctx)` or the callback-style generator where you pass a handler fn? differences in how ctx is threaded could explain this.

maria: iterator-style. the quickstart uses Next(ctx) which seems natural for newcomers, but it looks like the constructor spawns the handshake with a background ctx.

sam: workaround for now: call cancel() before Close() and drain any pending Next() calls. i.e. ensure you cancel the ctx passed into Next, then call gen.Close(). ugly but works. another option: call gen.Stop() (we have an internal stop) but it's not documented.

ci-bot: created issue #2345: "go-sdk: generator handshake ignores cancellation in iterator flow" — https://tracker/internal/2345 :white_check_mark:

leo: proposed API tweak for ergonomics: let Generator accept an initial ctx for the handshake so callers can bind lifecycle at creation time, e.g. `NewGenerator(ctx, opt...)` and also make `Close(ctx)` accept a ctx to avoid implicit background waits. small patch.

jen: i can draft a short quickstart patch and mention the cancel pattern in the README. onboarding notes: show both iterator and callback examples and call out cancellation best practices.

maria: thanks — i put a tiny repro gist here: https://gist.github.com/maria/handshake-repro. it includes a tiny test that fails with `go test -run TestHandshakeCancel`.

sam: sounding like a devex + eng-runtime joint fix. @leo can you sketch the constructor change? should be a 1-liner plus tests.

leo: yup — will open a draft PR that adds `WithHandshakeCtx(ctx)` option, and a test ensuring Close(ctx) doesn't hang if the handshake ctx is cancelled. also add a comment in generator.go about why we prefer passing ctx in.

jen: i'll update the quickstart and sample app once the PR lands. we should also add a short note in migration.md for older SDK versions. :+1:

maria: great. tagging this as high-onboard-friction in the issue. appreciate the quick triage! :raised_hands:
